exposure: Implementation of checklists for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HDP)
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rate
cohort: 763 women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with HDP
finding: Implementation of checklists for HDP improved adherence to national clinical guidelines and was associated with improved perinatal management, including reduced anti-hypertensive treatment, increased MgSO(4) utilization, prolonged gestation, decreased cesarean delivery rates, and lower NICU admission rates.
mod_finding: The rate of both elective and intrapartum cesarean delivery decreased after the implementation of the checklists.
